note: Spans are verbatim substrings of data/papers.json abstracts; scripts/verify_snapshot.py enforces this. Settings are paraphrased from the abstract only. expected_outcome, covers_our_setting, coverage_note, config_change and claims_speed are human-curated, never LLM-judged. Coverage criterion (same for every claim): covers_our_setting = the abstract states the result for Transformer language models, or for Transformers in general without restricting the task.

claims.method: Pre-LN Transformer trained without learning-rate warm-up
claims.setting: Transformers on a wide range of NLP applications (per abstract)
claims.claim: Pre-LN Transformers without the warm-up stage reach results comparable to baselines with less training time and tuning.
claims.source_span: We show in our experiments that Pre-LN Transformers without the warm-up stage can reach comparable results with baselines while requiring significantly less training time and hyper-parameter tuning on a wide range of applications.
claims.coverage_note: Abstract states the result for Pre-LN Transformers 'on a wide range of applications' (Transformers in general, task not restricted).

claims.setting: Transformers (theory, mean field analysis at initialization)
claims.claim: At initialization Post-LN has large expected gradients near the output layer, which is why warm-up is needed.
claims.source_span: we prove with mean field theory that at initialization, for the original-designed Post-LN Transformer, which places the layer normalization between the residual blocks, the expected gradients of the parameters near the output layer are large
claims.coverage_note: Theory stated for the Post-LN Transformer in general; no task restriction.

claims.method: Optimizer / LR-scheduler sensitivity of Transformer training
claims.claim: Transformer training needs carefully designed optimizers and LR schedulers; conventional SGD fails to train Transformers effectively.
claims.source_span: their training requires non-trivial efforts regarding designing cutting-edge optimizers and learning rate schedulers carefully (e.g., conventional SGD fails to train Transformers effectively)
claims.coverage_note: States the training difficulty for Transformers (NLP tasks), which includes language modeling.

claims.setting: several tasks with diverse network architectures (per abstract; RNNs are discussed)
claims.claim: RMSNorm achieves performance comparable to LayerNorm while reducing running time by 7%~64% on different models.
claims.source_span: RMSNorm achieves comparable performance against LayerNorm but reduces the running time by 7%~64% on different models
claims.coverage_note: Result stated for 'diverse network architectures' (RNNs emphasized); Transformers or language models not named.

claims.claim: RMSNorm is computationally simpler and more efficient than LayerNorm.
claims.source_span: RMSNorm is computationally simpler and thus more efficient than LayerNorm.
claims.coverage_note: Stated for neural networks in general; Transformers or language models not named.

claims.setting: SGD on CIFAR-10/100, EEG recordings, downsampled ImageNet
claims.claim: Warm restarts improve the anytime performance of SGD when training deep networks.
claims.source_span: we propose a simple warm restart technique for stochastic gradient descent to improve its anytime performance when training deep neural networks
claims.coverage_note: Evaluated on CIFAR, EEG and downsampled ImageNet; not Transformers.

claims.setting: Adam and SGD on image classification datasets
claims.claim: Decoupled weight decay substantially improves Adam's generalization performance.
claims.source_span: (ii) substantially improves Adam's generalization performance, allowing it to compete with SGD with momentum on image classification datasets
claims.coverage_note: Evidence is on image classification datasets; not Transformers.

claims.setting: computer vision, NLP and speech tasks (per abstract)
claims.claim: GELU shows performance improvements over ReLU and ELU across all considered tasks.
claims.source_span: find performance improvements across all considered computer vision, natural language processing, and speech tasks
claims.coverage_note: Reported across vision, NLP and speech tasks; Transformers or language models not named.

claims.claim: Some GLU variants give quality improvements over ReLU or GELU in the Transformer feed-forward sublayer.
claims.source_span: find that some of them yield quality improvements over the typically-used ReLU or GELU activations
claims.coverage_note: Abstract restricts the result to the Transformer sequence-to-sequence model, not language modeling or Transformers in general.

claims.setting: auto-regressive language modeling at 500M-1.9B parameters (T5/C4 per abstract)
claims.claim: Primer's gains are mostly attributed to squaring ReLU activations and adding depthwise convolutions to Q, K, V.
claims.source_span: Primer's improvements can be mostly attributed to two simple modifications: squaring ReLU activations and adding a depthwise convolution layer after each Q, K, and V projection in self-attention.
claims.coverage_note: Abstract states the result for Transformers on auto-regressive language modeling (scale differs; the criterion does not use scale).

claims.setting: auto-regressive language modeling, compute scale grows (per abstract)
claims.claim: Primer's gains over the Transformer increase as compute scale grows.
claims.source_span: Experiments show Primer's gains over Transformer increase as compute scale grows and follow a power law with respect to quality at optimal model sizes.
claims.coverage_note: States the scale trend for Transformers on auto-regressive language modeling.

claims.setting: transformer-based language models; long text classification benchmarks (per abstract)
claims.claim: RoFormer with RoPE consistently outperforms its alternatives on the evaluated benchmarks.
claims.source_span: Our experiments show that it consistently overcomes its alternatives.
claims.coverage_note: Abstract reports the empirical result on long text classification benchmarks, not language modeling.

claims.setting: large feedforward networks on small training sets; speech and object recognition
claims.claim: Random dropout gives big improvements on many benchmark tasks.
claims.source_span: Random "dropout" gives big improvements on many benchmark tasks and sets new records for speech and object recognition.
claims.coverage_note: Feedforward networks on speech and object recognition; not Transformers.
